skill.summary: Automatically fetch latest library/framework documentation for Claude Code via Context7 API
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives. The bash block documents a manual npx installation command, and the URL is a markdown link to GitHub examples. No prompt injection or semantic abuse was found in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 16-18 contain a fenced bash example for manual installation, not executable skill code. There is no script, hook, or automatic shell execution path in the scanned file.
Line 26 is a markdown link to a GitHub repository for examples. It does not define a runtime network request or data transmission behavior.

content.value_statement: AI coding sessions often use stale package knowledge. This skill prompts documentation lookup through Context7 for current library and framework guidance.
actual_capabilities: Prompts documentation research when users ask about libraries or frameworks.
Names React, Next.js, Prisma, and other popular libraries as suitable topics.
Supports natural use inside Claude Code conversations.
Uses Context7 as the stated documentation source.
Documents optional API key configuration for higher rate limits.
Provides a global installation command for the skill.
limitations: The skill file does not include implementation code or API configuration details.
Examples and troubleshooting are delegated to the linked GitHub repository.
Documentation quality depends on Context7 coverage for the requested library.
Optional API keys may be needed for higher usage limits.

use_cases.title: Check Framework Usage
use_cases.description: Ask for current React, Next.js, or Prisma guidance before changing application code.

use_cases.title: Reduce Stale Answers
use_cases.description: Use current documentation research when AI advice may depend on recent library releases.

use_cases.title: Compare Library Behaviors
use_cases.description: Request documentation-backed notes before selecting an API or migration path.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up Basic Usage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one library topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Context7 documentation to explain the current recommended way to use routing in Next.js.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Before Coding
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer wants current docs before making edits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before editing, check current Prisma documentation for transaction behavior and summarize the relevant guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Current APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Research current React documentation and compare the recommended patterns for useEffect and server components.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Version-Sensitive Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for changes that depend on recent docs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Context7 to research the latest Next.js migration guidance, then propose a step-by-step plan with risks and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Check the latest Prisma documentation for nested writes.
output_examples.output: A concise summary of current nested write behavior, key limitations, and recommended next steps for implementation.

output_examples.input: Research current Next.js routing guidance before changing this page.
output_examples.output: A documentation-backed explanation of the relevant routing model, followed by practical guidance for the requested change.

output_examples.input: Compare current React recommendations for effects and data loading.
output: Important caveats for effects and server rendering.
Suggested approach for the project context.

best_practices: Ask for the specific library, version, and feature area when possible.
Configure API keys through environment variables when higher limits are needed.
Request a short documentation summary before accepting code changes.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on it for private documentation that Context7 cannot access.
Do not treat fetched documentation as a substitute for project tests.
Do not ask broad questions when a focused package topic would work better.
